changes.rationale: Approved immutable lookup plus task binding now fits the demonstrated low-wait use case without deleting authority from the cache key. Cold misses and finite catalog recall remain important limits; no exceptional whole-workload fit claimed.

Within SDK wire/state contracts, final artifacts and independent audit satisfy their actual byte envelopes; legacy behavior and original rights are preserved. Full frozen bundles, small-public/large-private cases, invalid state/schema and source/epoch races are exercised. This scores observable contracts, not perfect semantic task coverage.

Origin resource/action identity remains strict while explicit scoped publication permits a new principal-owned binding. Foreign-origin audit, forged selections, epoch/approval/source changes, dependency forget and report execution bindings are checked.

Single-copy artifact projection resolves the demonstrated ordinary envelope failure; saturation still refuses actual oversized bundles and unavailable/changed sources. Host quotas remain bounded. No dependency-outage/load fleet claim.

One public packet projection is shared by settle and delivery, with separately authorized audit; the formerly repeated Build/body transport is removed for new consumers. Internal generator/audit representations and compatibility paths still cost maintenance.
Existing inference/source/authority/transaction/budget and rendering mechanisms serve approved reuse, task CLI, measured consumer, frozen replay and packaged SDK without a new agent framework.

Compatible approved reuse meets3s in30/30 observations, a real improvement from0/3 fresh requests. A request distribution including unsupported goals still has unproven cold completion and unknown coverage; whole-workload3s is not met.

The reuse path performs one compact selection and zero body generation; packet size and I/O are bounded. This fits the small demonstrated library. Latest-first candidate cutoff misses an older eligible record; catalog growth and cold generation remain limits.

Frozen suite records60 actual cloud choices, per-call timing/tokens, negative and pending outcomes, source validation and whole delivery. Replay/current-projection and cumulative-budget counterchecks exist. Six repeated scenarios and local source I/O do not establish a production distribution.

Public state, audit, selection assessment/receipt, held costs and phase timing expose ordinary delivery and miss outcomes. Saved evidence separates ready, pending and error, including all60 attempts; model attribution errors are retained.

Current public consumers retrieve a usable single bundle without duplicated internal data; compatible selections complete within3s and incompatible requests return an explicit generation path. SDK recovery/access tests hold; actual end-user deployment is unverified.
Pre-validated immutable Skill selection actually addresses low-wait reuse for registered applicable tasks; arbitrary new generation remains a different uncompleted path.

The target SDK owner has documented approval/selection/binding/delivery interfaces and exercised current consumer/replay paths to complete bundles. Real deployment onboarding/support cost remains unknown under adoption.
Observed useful-artifact completion and latency improve on the registered reuse path and reject unsuitable tasks. This is a prototype outcome, not a causal field-work or task-success advantage.

Saved Skill retrieval, direct ContextStill retrieval and background stores are credible alternatives. This SDK is now a viable implementation option for explicit version/approval/binding needs, without demonstrated superiority.

The prototype trades preparation and approval/integration work for measured fast access while preserving source/authority lifecycle. That is a viable internal selection condition; unknown tasks and simple static retrieval may favor alternatives.
Approved reuse, compact delivery, task binding and regression evidence are delivered. Cold3s, real host and sustained outcomes remain uncompleted rather than counted as delivery.

The revised scope reuses shared mechanisms, caps60 small calls within the existing cumulative15USD budget, preserves unknown costs and freezes conditions. Production dependencies and limits are reported instead of silently dropped.

Direct owner feedback about incomplete output, grading, tokens and latency led to measured changes and a changed architecture, with old failures preserved and positive/negative acceptance evidence. Actual field benefits remain unknown.
